The Offer
Morning nets. Karan Dhillon is laughing, signing autographs, throwing balls for the kids of the groundstaff. As if last night never happened.
Morning, champ. Front foot's a bit late today. Sleep well?
"Like a baby. Saw nothing, heard nothing."
Play along. For now.
"Who's threatening your family?"
Straight out.
Good. Sleep's important at your age.
Not here.
You're twenty-one and you've already been through one of these. Don't go through two. Bat. Eat. Sleep. That's all.
Saturday. Camp break. A message from a number you don't have.
Hi {first}! Ishita Bedi, sports management. 🙂
Car outside the academy gate at 7. Flight to Mumbai at 8. Dinner at 10.
Back before curfew. Trust me, you'll want to hear this.
Mumbai. A rooftop thirty floors up. The sea is black and the city is gold. A waiter puts down a mocktail that costs more than Papa makes in a day.
Let me be honest, because nobody else will be. In six weeks you'll either be a nobody from Rajgarh again, or the most marketable cricketer in India.
If it's the second one, you need me. One crore signing amount. Three brands. A shoe, a phone, a soft drink.
Your father gets a real shop. Your sister gets a real college. You get to only think about cricket.
One crore. Papa used to count coins at night to see if we could afford milk.
One small thing. Exclusive representation. All your media goes through us. Every interview, every post.
Every interview. Neha.
Sign tonight.
One crore. Don't overthink it.
Send the contract to Neha first.
She reads fine print for a living.
"I'll talk to my father first."
Slow down.
Hire Rocky's lawyer to read it tonight.
A real lawyer, on a Saturday night.
Of course. Family first. The offer's open till Monday. After that, it goes to Vikrant Chauhan.
She slides over a gold pen. Your signature looks different in Mumbai. Bigger.
Welcome to the family, {first}. Mr. Mehra will be so pleased.
...Mehra?
Page 14, clause 9(c).
The agency is 51% owned by Mehra Sports Group.
Raghav Mehra. The same name that keeps coming up in Sunny's court papers.
Don't sign. Don't drink anything. Come home.
At 1 AM the lawyer calls back. "Clause 9(c). The agency is majority-owned by Mehra Sports Group. And clause 14 lets them sell your image rights to anyone. Including people you've never met."
3:12 AM. Back in Bengaluru. Your phone won't stop vibrating. It's buzzing so hard it falls off the bed.
Bhai. Bhai, wake up. You're trending. You're number one.
A video. 2.4 million views in three hours.
It's you, two years ago, in a hotel lobby. Shaking Sunny Bhai's hand. Smiling.
The caption: "National camp probable caught with jailed bookie."
The photo in the envelope was a warning. The video is the price for ignoring it.
